title: Character Representation
body:
[[ASCII]]

Characters are stored as small integers. On the 68000 that means one [[ASCII]] code per
[[Byte]], so `'A'` and `65` and `$41` are the same eight bits and only your intent
distinguishes them. See [[Data representation]].

A string is then just a run of those bytes plus an agreement about where it ends: C uses a
terminating `$00`, the `dc.b` [[Directives|directive]] is how you lay one down in assembly.
